S0.desc: current: V3 driver (D0), ops of the frozen bitstream (V5 uses op2 only), key re-sent every call; ARM side as implemented (no session caching)

S1.desc: D1 fixed driver (cacheable buffers + cache maintenance), same op interface

S2.desc: S1 + public key resident in PL (NTT form) + fused encrypt-one-feature op (in m,u,e0,e1; out c0,c1); ARM side also caches NTT(a),NTT(b),NTT(s),residues(s) per session (fairness)

S3.desc: S2 + all fused features of a batch in ONE call (call coalescing)

S4.desc: S3 + D2 zero-copy user buffers (u-dma-buf like), DMA-bandwidth bound only

S5.desc: S3 with a stronger ARM baseline: NTT/INTT/pointwise 3x faster (NEON-NTT-like; sensitivity)

S6.desc: what-if: S4 + secret key resident in PL, fused decrypt d=c0'+c1'*s (security trade-off)

S7.desc: what-if: S4 + key-resident product-pair op K (in u; out b*u, a*u; adds stay on ARM) -- the interface suggested by Stone's min-cut

W1.desc: ARM-software what-if on S7 hardware: ternary residues by lookup, m residues by Barrett (ESTIMATED), session caches

W2.desc: W1 + ARM products as sparse-ternary convolutions (u,s have 64 nonzeros; no NTT) (ESTIMATED)

W3.desc: W1 + encode/decode 3x faster (hypothesis: per-coefficient std::pow twist dominates; UNMEASURED)
